title: practical-quant-multiplexing-scaling-workbook
summary: A working workbook that tests hybrid quantization + multiplexed batching heuristics across multi-region GPU fleets to estimate throughput, SLO burn, and quality delta for production planning.
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, working sheet used to estimate how mixing quantization levels and multiplexed batching strategies impacts net throughput, tail latency, and model output fidelity across regions. Intended for infra capacity planning for Dedicated + Hosted fleets when we want to push utilization without degrading customer-visible quality beyond a small delta.

Key ideas / definitions used here:
- Multiplexing: allowing multiple lightweight requests (short sequences) from different tenants to share a GPU context using packed batches and KV cache multiplex rules.
- Hybrid quantization: serving model variants at different numeric precisions (FP16, INT8, INT4-like simulated) depending on policy and fallbacks.
- Fidelity delta (FD): coarse metric defined here as the mean task-level quality drop vs FP16 baseline on our eval prompt set (higher = worse).
- SLO burn: expected probability of violating per-request latency SLO (95th ms) under a scenario.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model family: open-llm-ish 13B baseline. FP16 throughput on H100: 120 tokens/sec (single request, exclusive).
- Effective INT8 throughput on H100: +2.0x tokens/sec vs FP16 (tested microbench). Simulated low-precision (INT4-ish) +3.2x but with non-linear quality loss.
- Region fleet: NA (16 H100), EU (8 H100), APAC (6 A100). Mixed region latencies and burst allowances: NA burst +25%, EU +10%, APAC +5%.
- Typical request mix: 65% short (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (65-512), 10% long (512+).
- Prefix cache hit rate assumptions: 18% global baseline, can be improved to 28% with eviction tuning.
- Target 95th latency SLO: 250ms for short, 450ms for medium.

Scenarios evaluated (rows):
1) Baseline FP16 single-tenant (no multiplexing), conservative routing.
2) INT8 aggressive batching (pack to fill 4096 token window), low multiplexing concurrency.
3) Hybrid policy: short requests prefer INT8+multiplex, medium prefer FP16, long use FP16 with preemption.
4) INT4-simulated multiplex high-util: maximize throughput at cost of fidelity; used only for non-SLA customers.
5) Dynamic fallback policy: serve INT8 but auto-fallback to FP16 if confidence drop > threshold or eval prompts show FD > 0.015.

Representative sheet (summary numbers, region-aggregated):
- Scenario 1 (FP16 conservative)
  - Effective throughput (tokens/sec, fleet): 120 * 30 H100-equivalent = 3600 tok/s
  - Utilization headroom: 40% (safe ops)
  - FD: 0.0 (baseline)
  - 95th SLO burn: 4%

- Scenario 2 (INT8 aggressive batching)
  - Effective throughput: 3600 * 2.0 = 7200 tok/s (approx)
  - Utilization headroom: 15%
  - FD: 0.012 mean on eval prompts
  - 95th SLO burn: 9% (more tails due to microbursting + packing pauses)

- Scenario 3 (Hybrid policy)
  - Effective throughput: short paths +3.0x, medium/long ~1.1x -> net +1.9x vs baseline => ~6840 tok/s
  - Utilization headroom: 22%
  - FD: 0.006 overall (shorts contribute most of delta)
  - 95th SLO burn: 6% (acceptable for most tiers)

- Scenario 4 (INT4 high multiplex)
  - Effective throughput: baseline *3.2 => ~11520 tok/s
  - Utilization headroom: 3% (no headroom, brittle)
  - FD: 0.035 (some tasks break; not okay for core customers)
  - 95th SLO burn: 18% (tail risk high)

- Scenario 5 (Dynamic fallback)
  - Effective throughput: depends on workload; measured ~2.1x baseline in tests
  - FD: 0.004 after automatic rollbacks/fallbacks
  - 95th SLO burn: 5%

Region breakdown example (Hybrid policy, rough):
- NA (16 H100): nominal capacity at policy = 16 * 120 * 1.9 = ~3648 tok/s; target utilization 70% => target load 2550 tok/s.
- EU (8 H100): ~1824 tok/s nominal; target util 68% => target 1240 tok/s.
- APAC (6 A100 equiv ~0.85 H100): treat as 5.1 H100 eq => ~1162 tok/s nominal; target util 65% => target 755 tok/s.
Total planned target load ~4545 tok/s. Spare capacity for failover: ~15% shadow (hot spare) -> plan +680 tok/s.

Operational heuristics / knobs to tune:
- Pack window size: smaller windows reduce tail spikes but lower packing efficiency. Favor 256–1024 token windows for mixed traffic.
- Multiplex concurrency cap: cap concurrent multiplexed tenants per GPU to avoid KV eviction storms. Start with cap=8 and iterate.
- Prefix cache sizing: increase per-instance cache for regions with high short-request ratio (NA). Moving from 18% -> 28% cache hit reduces token work by ~7% fleet-wide.
- Opportunistic INT8: annotate routes that are low-risk for fidelity and allow INT8; keep SD (safety) routes pinned to FP16.
- Canary evaluation: always run a 1% shadow of requests to FP16 to measure live FD and trigger rollback when FD > 0.012 for 1h.

Failure modes and mitigations: 
- Mode collapse (quality spike after quantized kernel upgrade): mitigation -> staged rollout + golden-prompt regression suite + rollback flagging.
- Tail amplification when many small requests pack together: mitigation -> jitter arrival, strict per-tenant multiplex cap.
- Cross-region failover overload: mitigation -> pre-warmed reserved capacity + gradual spill policies.

Actionable capacity plan (next quarter):
1) Pilot hybrid policy on NA region: convert 30% of short routes to INT8 + multiplex, measure FD over 2 weeks.
2) Add 2 H100 equivalents to NA pool as hot spare for failover and increased packing headroom.
3) Tune prefix cache and observe hit rate delta; budget 1.5% cost for increased mem footprint.
4) Automate canary rollback triggered by FD > 0.012 for 1h or 95th latency > 1.5x SLO.
5) Run a weekend stress test simulating 3x short-request bursts with INT4-simulated pack to validate tail risk and autoscaler behavior.

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need a more robust per-route FD taxonomy (task types weigh differently). Should we track FD by customer cohort?
- What's the right incentive model for customers to opt into INT8 paths (discounts? telemetry)?
- Do we have telemetry coverage to detect microburst packing artifacts in time? (stash: INFRA-telemetry-coverage audit).

Raw worksheet excerpt (CSV-style lines for quick import to sheet):
scenario,region,hw_equiv_h100,nominal_tok_s,util_target,planned_load_tok_s,spare_tok_s,FD,95th_burn
baseline,NA,16,1920,0.60,1152,200,0.000,0.04
hybrid,NA,16,3648,0.70,2554,375,0.006,0.06
hybrid,EU,8,1824,0.68,1240,180,0.006,0.06
hybrid,APAC,5.1,1162,0.65,755,125,0.006,0.06
int8-aggressive,NA,16,3840,0.85,3264,80,0.012,0.09
int4-high,NA,16,5888,0.98,5760,0,0.035,0.18

Notes on numbers: these are back-of-envelope and derived from microbench runs (see linked PR). Use these to size purchase/commit conversations — do not sign contracts off these numbers without a week-long pilot.

Appendix: quick checklist for running pilot
- [ ] Create canary route set and tag low-risk customers
- [ ] Deploy INT8 kernels to canary nodes with feature-flag
- [ ] Run regression suite (golden prompts + adversarial set) before rollout
- [ ] Enable shadow FP16 copy for live FD telemetry
- [ ] Schedule weekend stress run and notify SRE

End of workbook.
